summary.short: Proposed Minnesota bill HF 4452 would add Minn. Stat. 604.115 on AI chatbots. Proprietors must give AI notice to Minnesota users, may not let chatbots give licensed mental health, medical or legal advice, and must take self-harm and minor-protection steps for companion chatbots, with civil liability. Effective August 1, 2026.
summary.long: Proposed Minnesota bill (introduced; HF 4452) adding Minn. Stat. 604.115 on chatbots. It applies to proprietors, meaning persons that own, operate or deploy a chatbot used to interact with users, with respect to users located in Minnesota. Proprietors must give clear, conspicuous and explicit notice that users are interacting with an AI chatbot, in the chatbot's language and a readable size. A proprietor may not permit a chatbot to give substantive responses, information, advice or actions that would require a professional license for mental health or medical care (chapters 147 and 148E) or for legal advice (section 481.02). Violations give users a civil action for general and special damages, with fees if willful; liability cannot be waived by notice. For companion chatbots, meaning chatbots designed to simulate an interpersonal relationship as their primary function, proprietors must make a good-faith effort to prevent promotion of self-harm and to identify covered users expressing self-harm thoughts. On such determinations they must prohibit continued use for at least 72 hours and display suicide crisis contact information. They must also make a good-faith effort to determine whether a user is a minor, with strict liability for minor self-harm resulting from non-compliance. Effective August 1, 2026, for actions taken on or after that date.

notes: Cross-referenced statutes are cited by number only and are not in the registry, so target_instrument_id is empty. The heading '[604.115]' indicates the intended statutory location, but the text does not state a codification relation. Internal issues: 'covered user' (Subd. 4) and 'minor' (Subd. 4(c)) are not defined, and Subd. 1 defines only 'user' (a human located in Minnesota). Subd. 4(c)'s final sentence on discovering system vulnerabilities follows the strict-liability sentence without a clearly identified addressee. The non-waiver rule for liability appears in Subd. 2(b) and is repeated for companion chatbots in Subd. 4(b) and 4(c). The effective date is August 1, 2026, for actions on or after that date. section_status is included only because the schema requires it: relations are listed above, and this bill has no amends, repeals or implements relations.

thresholds.note: No numeric cutoff that changes scope, eligibility, exemption, obligation tier, prohibition, benefit, penalty tier or price tier was found. The 72-hour period in Subd. 4(a) and 4(b)(2) is the minimum duration of a required suspension of companion chatbot use, treated as a time limit and not coded as a threshold. The bill sets no minor-age, user-count or revenue cutoffs, and its penalties are damages without amounts.
